shortQuestions: In the past people laughed with their hearts and eyes, shook hands with their hearts, and were sincere and warm-hearted; guests were truly welcome. Today people laugh only with their teeth, shake hands without warmth, search your pockets with cold eyes, and say 'come again' without meaning it — modern people are insincere, artificial and selfish.

The poet wants to learn from his young son how to laugh and smile genuinely again — to unlearn the artificial behaviour and false faces he has adopted, and to regain the innocence and sincerity of childhood.

'Laugh with their teeth' means a false, artificial smile that shows only teeth and no real feeling. 'Teeth like a snake's bare fangs' means that such a smile is dangerous and deceitful — it hides hostility and harm behind a pleasant look.
He compares their eyes to 'ice-block-cold eyes' — cold, cruel and lifeless — because modern people look at others without warmth, calculating and searching for their own benefit.
The tone is nostalgic, regretful and ironic, with a note of sadness about the loss of sincerity; it ends in a hopeful, humble tone as the poet asks his son to teach him to laugh again.

Stanza 1: 'they used to laugh with their hearts / laugh with their eyes' (metaphor of sincere laughter); 'ice-block-cold eyes' (metaphor). Stanza 4: 'I have learned to wear many faces like dresses' (simile) — home face, office face, street face, host face, cocktail face; 'conforming smiles like a fixed portrait smile' (simile).

s: Paraphrase of stanza 3: The poet says he has learned to say things he does not mean — 'Feel at home!' and 'Come again!' — and to shake hands and laugh without any real feeling. When guests come to his house again, he says the same words, but he does not wish them to come; it is only formal politeness.

Paraphrase of stanza 4: He says he has learned many things from society: to wear different faces like dresses for different places — at home, at the office, in the street, as a host and at parties — each with a fixed, artificial smile like a picture. He has also learned to laugh only with his teeth and to say 'Goodbye' when he means 'Good riddance'.
activities.n: The poet (Gabriel Okara) died in 2019, so the stanzas are paraphrased, not quoted.

activities: Debate guide — For modern times: technology, medicine, education, communication, comfort and opportunities. For the past: sincerity, strong family ties, simplicity, peace of mind, healthy food and environment, respect for elders. Each group should support points with examples; the teacher can conclude that we should combine modern progress with the sincerity of the past.
